The carbon nanotubes used in this study had a purity level of 96%.
The carbon nanotubes were used without any functionalization or additional processing.
The polyester resin was used as the matrix material, and a 3% hardener (methylethylketone peroxide) was added.
The mixing of the carbon nanotubes and polyester resin was done by mechanical mixing for 15 minutes.
The samples were prepared using a special mold to ensure proper placement in the waveguides of the network analyzer.
The XRD analysis confirmed the dimensional consistency of the received carbon nanotubes.
The SEM images showed a homogeneous and stable structure of the carbon nanotubes.
The saturation magnetization and coercivity values decreased with increasing carbon nanotube particle size.
The best radar absorption performance was observed in the composites with 48-78 nm carbon nanotubes, with a minimum reflection loss of -9.38 dB and an effective bandwidth of 10.27 GHz.
The improved radar absorption performance of carbon nanotube-reinforced composites is attributed to enhanced impedance matching, interfacial scattering, and dielectric and magnetic losses.
The study demonstrates the potential of using different particle sizes of carbon nanotubes to tune the absorption bands for various radar absorbing applications.
The research findings can serve as a guide for future studies on optimizing microwave absorption properties and using them in various applications.
The study highlights the importance of considering particle size as a key factor in the design of radar absorbing materials.
The use of carbon nanotubes in radar absorbing materials can contribute to the development of lightweight and highly efficient electromagnetic wave absorbing materials.
The study provides insights into the complex interaction between nanotechnology and radar absorbing materials, which is constantly expanding.
